title: The glucose readings aren't added in 5 minute intervals anymore
body: Hi, I use Dexcom G6 with xDrip+, it works very well but suddenly it started to add readings from 2 minutes to 8 minute intervals instead of 5 and its really visible and bothering me, i can still keep a good eye on my bloodsugar, but its really annoying. Does anyone know why it happens? Screenshot below to show what i mean, can easily see the dots arent added in 5 minute intervals anymore. Does anyone know why this suddenly started to happen? Edit: It suddenly fixed itself. Only thing i know did earlier tonight was to go to system status, forget device, force close app, clear cache, start xdrip+ again, and start source setup wizard to connect to my G6 again.

This is my take:

The time of a reading is divided by 2.5 minutes (FUZZER is a constant with a value representing 2.5 minutes).
`    public static final int FUZZER = (1000 * 30 * 5); // 2.5 minutes`
`        return new PointValue((float) (bgReading.timestamp / FUZZER), (float) unitized(bgReading.calculated_value));`

The result is later multiplied by 2.5 minutes.
`            final Long time = (real_timestamp > 0) ? real_timestamp : ((long) pointValue.getX()) * FUZZER;`

Before this multiplication, the fractional part of the division is discarded.
The result is used as the time of the reading.    
The effect is to place all readings on a 2.5-minute grid.  A consequence of this is that there will be a time shift of the readings on the graph only that could be anywhere between 0 to 2.5 minutes to the left (showing the reading at an earlier time than the real time).
If everything works as described, all readings should show up with a 5-minute spacing between them.

However, if the fractional part of the division is very close to either 0 or 1, a small time jitter could cause the integer part of the division to grow or shrink by 1 resulting in an unintended time shift of 2.5 minutes.  
Statistically speaking, most of the time we will be away from 0 or 1.  That's why this issue doesn't happen all the time.

If you are wondering how far you are from the boundary, tap on your last reading on screen and note the time.  Then, open the BG Data Table and look at the time of the last reading.  The difference between the two timings is something between 0 and 2.5 minutes.  If it is too close to 0 or 2.5 minutes, you could experience this issue.

Before we can consider making any changes, I'd like to know why the FUZZER scheme was introduced originally in March of 2015.  So, I have asked the question, and hopefully will hear back.

One solution I can think of is to reduce FUZZER from 2.5 minutes to 1 minute.  Then, we will still experience this behavior.  How

It turns out this issue had been noticed a long time ago:
https://github.com/StephenBlackWasAlreadyTaken/xDrip-Experimental/pull/288

I took the graph from the post by tolot27.  I identified the readings that had moved because of the unfortunate positioning of the readings with respect to the FUZZER bucket boundaries.
I used a spreadsheet to create a set that would visually look the same.  
![Screenshot 2021-06-09 143230](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/121409541-a2fbf800-c92f-11eb-9f96-6efdb1d01a0e.png)

Then, I changed the value of FUZZER to 0.  This is what it looks like.
![Screenshot 2021-06-09 143436](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/121409777-dcccfe80-c92f-11eb-8651-e7cec054b7e0.png)
You can see the distortion is gone.  I wish we could completely remove the FUZZER.  But, that is an extreme change to xDrip and very unlikely it will be accepted.

Then, I changed the FUZZER value to 1 minute (instead of 2.5 minutes).
![Screenshot 2021-06-09 143601](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/121410066-2e758900-c930-11eb-891b-528aa84ba091.png)

Then, I changed it to 30 seconds:
![Screenshot 2021-06-09 143830](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/121410242-6381db80-c930-11eb-9d3f-41709f5b091c.png)

We cannot forget that reducing the value of FUZZER will increase the probability of the issue occurring.  Reducing FUZZER from 2.5 minutes  to 30 seconds will increase the probability by a factor of 5.

I am going to open a PR reducing FUZZER to 30 seconds.  This will limit the error caused by the possible issue to something between 0 to 30 seconds.  Currently, the error can be anywhere between 0 to 2.5 minutes.
The probability will go up.  But, it is still almost unnoticeable at 30 seconds.    

Edit:
When I created those graphs using a spreadsheet, I overlooked the fact that the xDrip main screen only shows points placed on a 1-minute grid.  So, the graphs are not really representative of what will happen if we reduce the value of Fuzzer
Is the FUZZER also applied to Libre raw values which appear every minute? If yes, are there visual artefacts, too?

> Is the FUZZER also applied to Libre raw values which appear every minute? If yes, are there visual artefacts, too?

I believe so.  I say that based on my observation of an image I have copied from this issue: https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/pull/1303
and shown here:
![79228350-f082ef00-7e69-11ea-8e33-b8332267708a](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/121777376-b5f50f00-cb5f-11eb-8d09-d549b04a6dcb.png)

You can see that the raw value are bunched up together on a 2.5-minute grid.
If my PR is merged, they will appear on a 37.5-second grid.

You can now lower the fuzzer, to 37.5 seconds, in engineering mode by going to the advanced display settings and enabling the option at the very bottom.

That should address the issue reported here.

I have reopened this issue because the change I made to xDrip has not addressed the issue.
I am still working on this issue.

This is supposed to have been fixed with August 18, 2022.
https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2022.08.18

Please update to that release or any after that, and please report if you ever still experience the reported issue.
